name.text: Evaluate the Improper Integral and determine if it converges or diverges

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following integral and determine if it converges or diverges.

\(\displaystyle\int_{@lower_limit@}^{@w_pt@}\frac{{@coef_w*w@}}{\sqrt[3]{{@coef_w*w@}^{2}-{@const1@}}}\,dw=\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

Therefore, the integral is [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
worked solution

Since there is a discontinuity in the integrand at \(w ={@w_pt@}\), we can eliminate it by introducing a parameter as follows;

\[\displaystyle\int_{@lower_limit@}^ {@w_pt@}\frac{{@coef_w*w@}}{\sqrt[3]{{@coef_w*w@}^{2}-{@const1@}}}\,dw=\lim_{t \to {@w_pt@}^{-}} \displaystyle\int_{@lower_limit@}^t\frac{{@coef_w*w@}}{\sqrt[3]{{@coef_w*w@}^{2}-{@const1@}}}\,dw\]

because the interval of integration is [{@lower_limit@},{@w_pt@}].

Now we need to compute the integral \(\displaystyle\int_{@lower_limit@}^t\frac{{@coef_w*w@}}{\sqrt[3]{{@coef_w*w@}^{2}-{@const1@}}}\,dw\).

We can use \(u\)-substitution

Let \(\displaystyle u={@coef_w@}w^{2}-{@const1@}\). Then \( \displaystyle du={@diff((coef_w*w^2)-const1)@}\), so \(\displaystyle dw =\frac{du}{{@2*coef_w*w@}}\)

Recall that any time we make a \(u\)-substitution, the limits of integration change accordingly. For out case, we will have

\(w\) \(\rightarrow\) \(t\) :\(\quad\) \(u= \displaystyle {@expr_2@}\)

\(w\) \(\rightarrow\) {@lower_limit@} :\(\quad\) \(u={@expr_3@}\)

SO that our integral becomes

\[ \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{@lower_limit@}^t\frac{{@coef_w*w@}}{\sqrt[3]{{@coef_w@} w^{2}-{@const1@}}}\,dw&=\displaystyle\int_{@expr_3@}^{@expr_2@} {@func_2@} \,du \\ &= \left[ {@func_3@}\right]_{@expr_3@}^{@expr_2@}\\ &= {@func_5@} \end{align} \]

Therefore,

\[ \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{@lower_limit@}^{@w_pt@}\frac{{@coef_w*w@}}{\sqrt[3]{{@coef_w@}w^{2}-{@const1@}}}\,dw &=\lim_{t \to {@w_pt@}^{-}} \displaystyle\int_{@lower_limit@}^t\frac{{@coef_w*w@}}{\sqrt[3]{{@coef_w@}w^{2}-{@const1@}}}\,dw\\ &=\lim_{t \to{@w_pt@}^{-}} {@func_5@} \\ &={@ta_2@} \\ \end{align} \]

The integral is convergent if the associated limit exists and is a finite number and divergent if the associated limit either doesn't exist or is (plus or minus) infinity.

So in this case, the limit is {@mcq_correct(ta_3)[1]@}
